races.title: State Senate, District 41
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Caleb Theodros
cands.bio: Democrat who has served in the North Carolina State Senate for District 41 (part of Mecklenburg County) since January 2025. Former banker and community organizer. Studied economics and political science at UNC Charlotte. Placed third in the 2019 Charlotte City Council District 3 primary.

controversies.text: In 2024, primary runner-up Lucille Puckett challenged Theodros's residency. The county elections board unanimously dismissed it, saying he gave "substantial" evidence. He said he moved in July 2023 but updated his voter registration late. He also reported a GPS tracker on his car; police had no suspects.

endorsements.text: For 2026, Ballotpedia lists recommendations from several Sway voting-group voter guides, including Accessibility Rights for ALL, Beyond The Ballot, NC Public School Champions, and 'Reject AIPAC from City Council to Congress'. No organizational endorsements are listed for 2024.

cands.gaps: We found no stated positions from Theodros on data centers, property taxes, development and growth, land buying, immigration, policing, guns, abortion or school choice. His 2024 Ballotpedia survey names economic development, education and mental health as priorities and mentions attracting technology and new-age manufacturing jobs, with no specifics. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 survey. The list of bills he sponsored was empty on the page we read. We could not find his birthplace, the year his family arrived in the U.S., or the name of his banking employer or the dates of that work. We found no documented foreign ties.

local.label: Roots 90: Wikipedia says his family emigrated from Eritrea when he was a child and he grew up in Charlotte; his birthplace is not stated, and he ran for Charlotte City Council in 2019.

cands.name: Kevin Gray
cands.bio: Kevin Gray was the Republican nominee for North Carolina State Senate District 41 in 2026. He advanced without a primary and lost the general election to incumbent Democrat Caleb Theodros. We found no record of his jobs or any office he has held.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Kevin Gray was born, raised or when he moved to North Carolina. We found nothing on his career, education or any elected office. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey, and we found no campaign website, interviews or questionnaires stating his positions. We found no documented actions, public stances on development or data centers, controversies or endorsements.
